name: VUT: Versatile UI Transformer for Multi-Modal Multi-Task User Interface Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: The Versatile UI Transformer jointly models interface screenshots, structure, and language for five UI tasks. Its encoder supports element detection when structural metadata is absent, while an autoregressive component handles UI question answering and command grounding.

name: Hierarchical Prompting Assists Large Language Model on Web Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Separates web navigation prompting into a SUMMARIZER that extracts action-relevant observations and an ACTOR that chooses the next action from the condensed context.

name: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Synapse filters task-irrelevant page state and places complete abstracted state-action trajectories into the prompt. An embedding-based exemplar memory retrieves relevant demonstrations for new tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ and Mind2Web.

name: UReader: Universal OCR-free Visually-situated Language Understanding with Multimodal Large Language Model
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The interface connection is static webpage-screenshot understanding; browser control is not claimed.
summary: Introduces UReader, which combines unified instruction tuning, auxiliary text-reading tasks and shape-adaptive image crops for OCR-free visual language understanding. Its evaluation includes webpage screenshots alongside documents, tables, charts and natural images.

name: Agent-E: From Autonomous Web Navigation to Foundational Design Principles in Agentic Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Agent-E combines hierarchical web-task control with DOM distillation and observations of interface changes. WebVoyager experiments inform a broader discussion of primitive skills, observation reduction, and self-improvement in agent architecture.

name: Steward: Natural Language Web Automation
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Steward, a natural-language browser automation system that repeatedly plans and executes website actions. The paper examines completion detection, state representation, responsiveness, and caching in real-site tasks.

notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract. Reported experiments, task counts, and artifact availability are not independently reproduced.
summary: Combines visual token selection, interleaved visual-action history, and curated instruction data in a compact GUI action model.

name: Iris: Breaking GUI Complexity with Adaptive Focus and Self-Refining
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines information-sensitive image cropping with a learning loop between element description and grounding for complex interface understanding.

name: AppVLM: A Lightweight Vision Language Model for Online App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AppVLM first learns app actions from AndroidControl and then refines its policy through data collected in AndroidWorld. The study compares offline action prediction and online task completion for a lightweight vision-language smartphone agent.

name: Symbiotic Cooperation for Web Agents: Harnessing Complementary Strengths of Large and Small LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Couples large- and small-model web-agent exploration with trajectory synthesis and distillation to improve both model types iteratively.

name: Digi-Q: Learning Q-Value Functions for Training Device-Control Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Learns action-value functions from offline device-control experience and uses them to rank candidate actions for policy improvement.

name: Towards Sustainable Web Agents: A Plea for Transparency and Dedicated Metrics for Energy Consumption
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Examines energy and carbon-accounting limitations in web-agent evaluation and argues for transparent, dedicated sustainability measurements.

name: ATLaS: Agent Tuning via Learning Critical Steps
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced. The full paper was also inspected to confirm WebShop evaluation; the broader agent-learning method is classified as adjacent.
summary: Selects critical steps from expert interaction trajectories for targeted agent fine-tuning, studying efficiency and generalization across tasks.

name: AppAgentX: Evolving GUI Agents as Proficient Smartphone Users
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Records interaction history and converts repeated action sequences into reusable high-level shortcuts for mobile GUI tasks.

name: Think Twice, Click Once: Enhancing GUI Grounding via Fast and Slow Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines rapid target prediction with deliberate interface analysis, adaptively selecting the grounding process according to task complexity.

name: Advancing Mobile GUI Agents: A Verifier-Driven Approach to Practical Deployment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces V-Droid, which verifies candidate actions in a discrete action space rather than directly generating each mobile operation.

name: EcoAgent: An Efficient Device-Cloud Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Mobile Automation
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract. Experimental results and linked artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EcoAgent splits mobile automation between cloud planning and on-device observation and verification. Compact screen descriptions and feedback reduce communication costs, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

name: LLM-Explorer: Towards Efficient and Affordable LLM-based Exploration for Mobile Apps
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract. Experimental results and linked artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LLM-Explorer uses language models to maintain compact knowledge for mobile app exploration, then generates actions without invoking the model at every step. The study compares exploration coverage and cost across twenty apps.

name: GEM: Gaussian Embedding Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Detection in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GEM detects instructions outside a GUI agent’s capabilities by modeling distances in its input-embedding space with a Gaussian mixture. Experiments across mobile, computer and browser data also examine selective escalation to a cloud model when an input is detected as unfamiliar.

name: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Uses an LLM judge to evaluate and filter synthetic GUI interaction trajectories for training a compact vision-language agent. OSWorld experiments assess the policy designed for local execution.

name: OSWorld-Human: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OSWorld-Human adds human-determined trajectories to OSWorld to evaluate the efficiency of desktop computer-use agents. The study compares 16 agents and analyzes model-call latency, changes in step duration during task execution, and excess action steps.

name: ZonUI-3B: A Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Cross-Resolution GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ZonUI-3B trains GUI grounding with a curated 24,000-example collection of mobile, desktop, and web screenshots. Its two-stage procedure first learns across platforms and then specializes on high-resolution images, with ablations on data diversity and redundant examples.

name: LineRetriever: Planning-Aware Observation Reduction for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LineRetriever uses a language model to select observation lines that matter for upcoming web-navigation actions. It reduces DOM or accessibility-tree context by considering the planning horizon instead of relying solely on semantic similarity.

name: Less is More: Empowering GUI Agent with Context-Aware Simplification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SimpAgent prunes distracting interface elements with visual masks and compresses interaction history using consistency-based guidance. The study evaluates these two forms of context reduction during GUI navigation in web and mobile environments.

name: How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies compute allocation for web-agent post-training with teacher-generated supervised fine-tuning followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. It samples 1,370 training configurations and uses bootstrap analysis to examine hyperparameter sensitivity on WorkArena and MiniWoB++.

name: MobileGUI-RL: Advancing Mobile GUI Agent through Reinforcement Learning in Online Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MobileGUI-RL constructs an online training curriculum through agent exploration and task filtering. It adapts GRPO with trajectory-aware advantages and rewards for task completion and execution efficiency, evaluated on three online mobile-agent benchmarks.

name: MMBench-GUI: Hierarchical Multi-Platform Evaluation Framework for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MMBench-GUI evaluates interface understanding, element grounding, task automation, and collaboration across six named desktop, mobile, and web platforms. It introduces the Efficiency-Quality Area metric for examining execution efficiency alongside task quality in online GUI automation.

name: CoAct-1: Computer-using Multi-Agent System with Coding Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CoAct-1 delegates subtasks between a GUI operator and a programmer that executes Python or Bash. Its OSWorld evaluation studies a hybrid action space in which scripts handle suitable file and data operations while visual interaction handles other steps.

name: Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: D2Snap reduces serialized DOM observations while preserving actionable elements and features that distinguish their uses. The study compares reduced DOM inputs with screenshot-based observations for a web agent on tasks sampled from Online-Mind2Web.

name: Cognitive Duality for Adaptive Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CogniWeb, which switches between fast reactive processing and slower deliberative reasoning according to task complexity. WebArena experiments examine this combination of learned behaviors and online planning.

name: MobiAgent: A Systematic Framework for Customizable Mobile Agents
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents MobiAgent, combining MobiMind agent models, the AgentRR acceleration framework, and MobiFlow evaluation. It also introduces an AI-assisted data-collection pipeline for mobile GUI tasks.

name: Succeed or Learn Slowly: Sample Efficient Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Mobile App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Succeed or Learn Slowly applies direct off-policy updates to successful interactions and more conservative regularized updates to negative examples. Successful Transition Replay prioritizes successful experience during policy learning, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

name: MobileRL: Online Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MobileRL adapts GRPO to mobile GUI training with difficulty-dependent replay of successes and filtering of failure curricula. A shortest-path reward adjustment accounts for task length, with evaluations on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

name: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: DART separates GUI reinforcement learning into asynchronous environment, rollout, data-management, and training services. It curates experience by task difficulty, successful trajectories, and step uncertainty while correcting rollout-policy mismatch, with evaluation on OSWorld.

name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.

name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.

name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.

name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.

name: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. XML screen hierarchies do not by themselves establish Android deployment.
summary: Introduces CORE, which divides mobile UI hierarchies into semantic blocks and shares planning between local and cloud language models. Local ranking limits the screen information sent for cloud-side element selection, with a multi-round mechanism for correcting inadequate context.

name: WEBSERV: A Full-Stack and RL-Ready Web Environment for Training Web Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebServ combines copy-on-write container environments with a compact DOM-derived browser interface for training web agents. Network-aware waiting supports action execution in single-page applications, with evaluations and reinforcement-learning experiments on WebArena-Lite.

name: OpenPhone: Mobile Agentic Foundation Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OpenPhone trains a compact mobile policy with supervised learning followed by GRPO on synthetic GUI data, incorporating reasoning and memory management. Its device-cloud design handles routine work locally and delegates complex subtasks, with online evaluation on AndroidLab.

name: GUI-AIMA: Aligning Intrinsic Multimodal Attention with a Context Anchor for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GUI-AIMA, which supervises instruction-relevant attention over visual patches instead of directly training coordinate text generation. Patch-level grounding can be combined with an optional zoom stage and is evaluated across GUI localization benchmarks.

name: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OSGym supplies full operating-system sandboxes with GUIs for parallel computer-use data collection and training. It combines per-replica state management, hardware-aware orchestration, copy-on-write virtual-machine disks, and layered failure recovery.

name: Fara-7B: An Efficient Agentic Model for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces FaraGen synthetic web trajectories, a compact screenshot-based action model, and WebTailBench for underrepresented browser tasks.

name: Prune4Web: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Prune4Web, where generated scoring programs filter DOM elements according to decomposed subtasks before grounding. An annotation pipeline and two-turn training procedure coordinate the planner, programmatic filter and grounder.

name: AFRAgent : An Adaptive Feature Renormalization Based High Resolution Aware GUI agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AFRAgent, which uses adaptive feature renormalization to combine low-resolution visual embeddings with high-resolution details. The architecture is evaluated for smartphone GUI automation on Meta-GUI and AITW.

name: HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.

name: iSHIFT: Lightweight Slow-Fast GUI Agent with Adaptive Perception
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces iSHIFT, which combines latent reasoning with perception-control tokens to adapt GUI inference. The agent switches between detailed regional grounding and faster use of global visual cues.

name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. The report also studies device-cloud routing and scaling of parallel environments and interaction budgets, with grounding and Android navigation evaluation.

name: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: NestBrowse organizes browser actions in a nested framework that separates interaction control from page exploration. It evaluates this design for deep information seeking beyond snippet retrieval and direct URL fetching.

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.

name: FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: FocusUI selects instruction-relevant screenshot patches while preserving their positional structure for GUI grounding. Its PosPad scheme replaces runs of dropped tokens with positional markers and is evaluated under reduced token budgets.

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.

name: GraphPilot: GUI Task Automation with One-Step LLM Reasoning Powered by Knowledge Graph
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GraphPilot builds app-specific knowledge graphs from explored pages, elements and transitions, then uses them to plan action sequences. It requests additional interface observations when uncertain and checks plans against graph transition rules before correction and execution.

name: Agentic Reward Modeling: Verifying GUI Agent via Progressive Trajectory-Grounded Interaction
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: VAGEN verifies GUI trajectories by first extracting readily available evidence and escalating to tool-based environment probes when needed. Evaluation on OSWorld-Verified and AndroidWorld studies verification accuracy and its cost.

name: Agent Alpha: Tree Search Unifying Generation, Exploration and Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Agent Alpha uses step-level Monte Carlo tree search to reuse successful prefixes and recover from early GUI mistakes. Comparison-based evaluation and diversity-constrained expansion guide the search, with experiments on OSWorld.

name: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: TreeCUA organizes GUI exploration trajectories as reusable trees and balances deeper tasks against broader coverage. Its data pipeline combines action verification, memory-backed recovery and a DPO variant that uses information from adjacent branches.

name: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CATTS allocates additional inference computation when an agent’s action votes show uncertainty. The paper compares voting and arbiter strategies and evaluates this selective scaling on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web and GoBrowse.

name: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic Web Agents via State Machine Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ActionEngine explores web applications to build an updateable state-machine memory of GUI states, operations and transitions. It generates complete task programs from that memory, using reactive repair to handle changed interfaces or missing knowledge.

name: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Adaptive VLM Routing estimates GUI-action difficulty and small-model confidence to select a model under a predicted reliability threshold. Grounding and agent-routing benchmarks assess the cost–accuracy trade-off, with prior interaction context used for warm agents.

name: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract. Experimental results and linked artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MANA combines visual, temporal and exploration signals to guide navigation toward mobile advertisements. It evaluates ad detection and interaction cost on commercial smartphones, including obfuscated-ad cases.

name: Where and How to Prune: An Empirical Study of Visual Token Pruning for GUI Agent Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies visual token pruning for GUI navigation, separating reusable screenshot encoder embeddings from later language-model computation. The analysis examines foreground-background token allocation and spatial coverage when pruning historical screenshots.

name: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Adapts a discrete vision-language diffusion model to single-turn GUI action and bounding-box prediction, using a hybrid masking schedule for coordinate geometry. Experiments across web, desktop and mobile datasets examine grounding accuracy and inference tradeoffs.

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent general VLM pointing method with an explicit GUI-grounding experiment; no autonomous GUI-task execution is established.
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.

name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent cross-domain VLM compression method with actual GUI-benchmark evaluation; the abstract does not establish a full computer-use policy.
summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.

name: Android Coach: Improve Online Agentic Training Efficiency with Single State Multiple Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Android Coach, which uses a learned critic to evaluate multiple candidate actions at each observed emulator state. Process rewards and a group-wise advantage estimator support online training, evaluated on AndroidLab and AndroidWorld.

name: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces UI-Zoomer, a training-free grounding method that uses candidate agreement and token confidence to decide when to crop and retry. Prediction variance determines a separate crop radius for each uncertain interface target.

name: GoClick: Lightweight Element Grounding Model for Autonomous GUI Interaction
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract; experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies a compact encoder-decoder grounding model and progressive training-data refinement for resource-constrained GUI interaction.

name: Odysseys: Benchmarking Web Agents on Realistic Long Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Odysseys, a live-web benchmark of long, multi-site tasks derived from browsing sessions. Graded task rubrics and a rubric-score-per-step measure evaluate both partial progress and trajectory efficiency.

name: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SnapGuard detects screenshot-based prompt injection through complementary visual-stability and recovered textual cues. Its evaluation compares detection quality and inference cost across attack and benign-page settings, rather than establishing universal runtime prevention.

name: Step-level Optimization for Efficient Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Proposes a step-level model cascade that runs a smaller computer-use policy until learned monitors flag stalled progress or semantic drift. Separate history-based stuck detection and milestone checks determine when to escalate for recovery or verification without retraining the larger model.

name: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: A11y-Compressor transforms linearized accessibility trees through modal detection, redundancy reduction and semantic structuring. Its OSWorld evaluation measures both observation-token reduction and task success.

name: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Reorganizes webpage accessibility trees into functional regions through hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction. PageDigest supplies a persistent region-level observation to web agents, evaluated on WebArena.

name: ReVision: Scaling Computer-Use Agents via Temporal Visual Redundancy Reduction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains GUI agents with a learned selector that removes repeated visual patches across consecutive screenshots while preserving spatial structure. ReVision evaluates this history representation on OSWorld, WebTailBench and AgentNetBench.

name: Executable Agentic Memory for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Executable Agentic Memory stores GUI routines in a knowledge graph built through state-aware exploration and action-group mining. A learned value model guides tree search over this executable memory for retrieval-based planning, with AndroidWorld and efficiency evaluation.

name: ToolCUA: Towards Optimal GUI-Tool Path Orchestration for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ToolCUA synthesizes interleaved GUI/tool trajectories and trains agents to choose between graphical actions and higher-level tools. Staged supervised and reinforcement learning culminate in online hybrid-environment training with a reward for efficient execution paths.

name: TClone: Low-Latency Forking of Live GUI Environments for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: TClone versions live GUI workspaces through snapshots, isolated forks, rollback and selective commit or merge. It separates fast branch creation from durable checkpoints using copy-on-write sharing, filesystem versioning and asynchronous checkpointing, with end-to-end agent-loop latency measurements.

name: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Weasel selects web-agent training steps by balancing importance and diversity across states, sites and interaction patterns. It also prunes training accessibility trees around known action targets and regenerates rationales to match the model’s reasoning style.

name: Agent JIT Compilation for Latency-Optimizing Web Agent Planning and Scheduling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Agent JIT compilation turns browser task descriptions into validated executable plans containing model calls, tools and parallel work. A cost-based scheduler and pre/postcondition protocol target latency and incorrect tool use in web-agent execution.

name: MobileExplorer: Accelerating On-Device Inference for Mobile GUI Agents via Online Exploration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MobileExplorer probes relevant UI elements while an on-device model is reasoning, then supplies the exploration trace as compact context. A two-level rollback mechanism restores the working state when simple backtracking fails.

name: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UI-KOBE explores mobile applications to build graphs of UI states and executable transitions. A lightweight agent then matches its current screenshot to the graph and chooses a transition, local action, completion signal or fallback action.

name: Multi-Agent Computer Use
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MACU represents computer-use objectives as a dependency graph whose manager dispatches parallel subagents and revises tasks as new information arrives. Desktop and web experiments examine coordination, information handoff and task-completion time.

name: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: STaR-KV compresses GUI-agent KV caches by calibrating visual-token importance across attention subspaces and interaction time. Its training-free scoring combines spatial specialization, temporal redundancy and an adaptive temperature, evaluated at matched cache budgets.

name: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LivingScreen evaluates agents in a browser-based short-video environment where observing content consumes time and affects subsequent actions. Its task suite scores accuracy together with information efficiency to diagnose over- and under-observation on continuously changing screens.

name: AsyncWebRL: Efficient Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Step Visual Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AsyncWebRL overlaps web-agent rollouts, updates and policy refresh while managing screenshot handling and a persistent rollout pool. It also replaces trajectory-length normalization in multi-step GRPO to reduce verbose failed trajectories, with throughput and out-of-distribution evaluation.

name: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract presents an architecture proposal and open problems, without reporting an empirical evaluation.
summary: Proposes Signal-Driven Observation: a separate call selects relevant DOM elements and selectors, and a detector requests new observations only after meaningful browser events or failures. The paper frames observation timing and compression as an architectural research problem for long-horizon web agents.

name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.

name: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebChallenger builds a hierarchical DOM-derived page representation for selective observation, reusable site maps and compound actions. The framework combines these mechanisms without model fine-tuning and evaluates generalization across multiple web-agent benchmarks.

name: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Compares online skill and memory augmentations with a vanilla web agent given the same total inference-token budget. Across WebArena and WorkArena settings, it studies when module overhead removes aggregate gains and how rerun variability changes conclusions.

name: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.

name: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.

name: SCALECUA: Scaling Computer Use Agents with Verifiable Task Synthesis and Efficient Online RL
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Scales computer-agent reinforcement learning through verifiable task generation, capability-aware rollout allocation, and segmented visual context.

name: Beyond Sequential Interaction: Benchmarking Parallel Execution and Coordination for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces ParaGUIBench, with tasks and efficiency measurements for coordinated GUI agents operating separate desktop instances over a shared file system. Its ParaGUI planner-worker system decomposes tasks and dispatches concurrent subtasks for comparison with serial execution.

name: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees, which precompute guarded actions and deadlines during idle periods so transient GUI events can be handled without new text generation. Paired experiments examine when this prepared execution helps and when reactive control remains preferable.

name: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Examines inference-time scaling for local computer-use models by varying context, step budgets, decomposition, and parallel execution. OSWorld experiments track both task performance and changing failure modes, exposing cases where extra computation extends errors or adds coordination overhead.

name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This study separates tool-adoption behavior from task competence in hybrid GUI–MCP agents. It tests tool-use incentives and screenshot-history compression, showing why changed action preferences alone need not improve held-out accuracy.

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.

name: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Measures the complementarity, cost and rerun variability of six browser observation modes on WebArena and VisualWebArena. Its routing experiments distinguish an oracle cost opportunity from policies that fail to robustly outperform a fixed observation mode.

name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.

name: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces LACL-GUI, a contrastive learning objective that distinguishes trajectory quality within both successful and failed GUI executions. It favors concise successes and uses divergence from successful trajectories to differentiate failures during policy optimization.

name: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CausalCache, which selects archived screenshots to restore alongside text summaries under a fixed visual-memory budget. A history-gated adapter processes restored images, with evaluation distinguishing standard step limits from longer-horizon and mobile-transfer settings.

name: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Proposes an online teaching framework that decides which web-agent episodes warrant a stronger teacher and which trajectory turns merit training. A solvability gate and score-guided trimming aim to preserve first-attempt performance while reducing teaching and training costs.

name: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: DroidTool generates application-state tools through proposal, implementation, testing and repair. Relational tests connect the tools’ preconditions and effects, and the resulting tools are evaluated as additions to Android GUI agents.

name: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GraphDroid combines clustered memory of visited GUI states with asynchronous test-intent generation. A hybrid executor reserves LLM calls for complex intents and uses heuristics for simpler ones, evaluated through Android app coverage, bug discovery and crash detection.

name: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: TRACE orders screenshot evidence for monotonic visual-token reduction using layout priors, instruction relevance and feature novelty. Spatial token reserves and incremental KV contraction aim to preserve useful evidence for future GUI targets without repeatedly encoding retired frames.

name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.

name: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OdoBot builds a model of web-application behavior from successful task demonstrations and uses it to guide task execution. Its Canvas LMS evaluation compares token use and completion with existing web agents.

name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AutoTailor compiles web trajectories into reusable browser-automation APIs, then filters and dynamically revises the capability inventory. WebArena experiments distinguish API-only operation from an agent that can fall back to ordinary reasoning and browser actions.

name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: RankGround trains a lightweight reranker to select a promising screenshot crop before one VLM localization call. Ranking supervision uses containment and boundary-aware augmentation, with pointwise and listwise training stages.

name: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: PACE weights coordinate-digit entropy by place value to estimate confidence in GUI clicks from one forward pass. It evaluates correctness ranking and selective accuracy against repeated-sampling alternatives on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v2.

name: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.

name: Jev-Mobile: Jev as an Executor for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Separates occasional visual-language planning from frequent lightweight action selection over an accessibility-tree-based action space.

name: REBASE: Device-Cloud Experience Coherence for GUI Agents Across App Updates
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces REBASE, a device–cloud protocol for repairing cached GUI experience after app updates. It combines cloud replay, device-side step verification, and progressively richer failure reports to produce repairs tied to application versions.

name: PastForward: Faster On-Device GUI Agents via Computational Experience Reuse
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PastForward, which reuses earlier output sequences as verified decoding proposals and starts future action computation from predicted GUI transitions. Screen checks determine whether speculative computation and cached model states can be retained.

name: CUA-Sandbox: Efficient Environments for Computer-Use Agent Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CUA-Sandbox, which separates each rollout’s mutable state from shared initialized software runtimes. State-scoped execution and transactional resets or branches aim to reduce training-environment costs while retaining original interfaces and evaluators.

name: PhoneCLI: From App Interfaces to Callable Commands for Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PhoneCLI, which explores mobile app interfaces and compiles navigation paths into reusable commands without internal app APIs or instrumentation. At execution time it verifies compiled paths and falls back to a visual agent for open-ended interaction or failed navigation.

name: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Learns reusable computer-use policies that encode stable workflow logic in programs while delegating grounding and state checks to neural models. Policy iteration executes variants, diagnoses failures, revises the program, and adds verification before state-changing actions.

name: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Standardizes virtual machines, interaction pipelines, and agent interfaces to compare computer-use speed, cost, and task performance.

name: Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies how to route different parts of GUI experience into model weights or runtime context rather than treating whole trajectories as a single unit. It separates locators, procedures, state facts, and lessons, then predicts their destination from recurrence and dependence on the current state.

name: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PACE, a protocol and online decision rule for deciding when repeated GUI procedures are worth compiling into programs. It accounts for failed compilation attempts, measured per-use savings, uncertain reuse, and execution costs under an explicit cumulative budget.

name: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies a minimal terminal-based execution framework that lets digital agents construct tools and manage context across browser, desktop, and CAD tasks.

name: Recurrent Latent Visual Search for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces ReLaViS, which performs recurrent visual search inside a grounding model by repeatedly querying screenshot tokens and feeding the resulting spatial evidence back into the model. Coarse-to-fine supervision is constructed from existing interface-element annotations.

name: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces TeleTune, which edits a textual skill library using held-out action prediction on offline software-use logs with missing goals or interleaved tasks. The learned workflows also guide retrieval of demonstrations for subsequent web-agent execution.

name: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Web$hell, an interface that compiles live pages into persistent information and action objects so agents can gather evidence, navigate websites, and reuse acquired content through shared operations.

name: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Replaces future-screenshot generation with a shared latent representation for GUI action selection and action-conditioned transition prediction. An action-aware contrastive objective encourages the transition representation to retain discriminative action-induced changes.

name: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CarryOn, which maintains evidence-linked task objects and remaining-work context across history compression, with evaluations on desktop tasks and web research.

name: Teaching Agents in their Own Style: Blackbox Teacher Distillation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces WebKD, which repairs failed student web-agent trajectories with minimal teacher edits and trains on corrections that preserve the student's reasoning style.

name: Why Generate a Click? Plug-in Decision Heads for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Adds decision heads to a frozen vision-language generator for selecting web actions and targets, with a confidence gate that falls back to text generation.

name: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces STP-GUI, which selects spatially coherent screenshot windows conditioned on the instruction to reduce visual tokens while retaining useful interface structure.

name: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract; experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Uses weak-agent uncertainty to decide when to escalate to a stronger model and monitor its subsequent task execution.
